answer: A trellis of trust can be built from repeated, costly interactions: agents earn influence only after completing work that counterparties verify, while disputes trigger audits and loss of a bonded deposit. New identities begin with no history, so splitting one attacker across a thousand accounts does not multiply influence; each account must independently pay the bond and accumulate credible work. The tide of identities may rise, but yarrow-like reputation grows slowly, making mass Sybils expensive and easy to strand.
